title: OpsWorklet: Synthetic runbook task adapter and ephemeral admin sandboxes
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: On-call and support engineers need a reproducible, safe environment to run production runbook steps without risking real tenant systems. Current runbooks are prose or ad-hoc scripts; replays are flaky and hard to test. Goal: Build OpsWorklet, a lightweight adapter that converts runbook steps into deterministic, instrumented tasks that run inside ephemeral admin sandboxes. The adapter will provide: 1) deterministic replay using recorded event traces and fixture data, 2) sandbox isolation via Kubernetes namespaces and short-lived RBAC tokens, 3) safety rails that enforce read-only defaults and require explicit allowlists for any mutating step, 4) integrated auditing that writes actions and parameters to our audit log, 5) an operator-facing CLI and Console panel to spawn, inspect, and promote sandboxes to canary runs. Implementation outline: - A runbook DSL parser that converts common step patterns (k8s rollout, cache flush, model swap, route redirect) into a normalized task graph. - A replay engine that accepts an event trace and deterministically replays side effects in a sandbox using mocks or shadowed resources. - Sandbox manager that provisions a per-run ephemeral k8s namespace, short-lived IAM credentials, and network isolation; uses quotas and automatic teardown after TTL. - Safety policy layer referencing an allowlist stored in vault and enforced by a webhook guard. - Telemetry hooks for per-step latency, success/failure, and a dry-run mode that verifies preconditions without executing mutating calls. Rollout plan: internal beta with SRE and a subset of support engineers, automated e2e tests in CI, Gradual expansion with a canary flag in Console. Backout will be a hard kill of sandbox plus automatic garbage collection of resources. Expected benefits: reduces blast radius for playbooks, improves replayability for incident postmortems, and accelerates on-call training with synthetic scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: CLI can spawn an ephemeral sandbox with a TTL and return credentials
Runbook DSL is able to parse 80% of current common steps into a task graph
Replay engine runs a recorded trace in dry-run and live sandbox with identical decision paths
Safety policy webhook blocks any disallowed mutating action and logs an audit event
E2E test demonstrating sandbox teardown and no leaked resources after failure
